item.title: Trump announces ‘biggest oil deal in world history’ with Venezuela
item.description: US president says deal secures majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela.

item.title: Tuareg rebels free more Malian soldiers in prisoner swap, sources say
item.description: Tuareg rebels have freed about 60 Malian soldiers in exchange for one of their own leaders, security sources said.

item.title: Gunfire, blasts heard in several areas of Niger capital Niamey
item.description: Shots were heard around the city's Diori Hamani international airport and near the presidential palace.

item.title: Board of Peace’s Mladenov warns Gaza could be ‘gone for good’
item.description: Top envoy for the US-led Board of Peace says Gaza is at risk of being ‘gone for good’ without reconstruction.

item.title: US revises statements suggesting Chinese hackers attacked agencies
item.description: US Justice Department clarifies that the US Senate and Federal Reserve were targets but were not successfully hacked.

item.title: US judge rejects Trump’s bid to switch hush-money case to federal court
item.description: The US president has sought to overturn his criminal conviction for falsifying business records, citing immunity.

item.title: Iran war live: IRGC asserts strait control, US enforces blockade
item.description: Iran's IRGC claims decisive control over the Strait of Hormuz as the US maintains its naval blockade.

item.title: Cambodia’s claim to have ended scam compounds met with scepticism
item.description: Cambodia's claim of eradicating its scam compounds met with scepticism from Amnesty International and industry experts.

item.title: Spain asks EU for help to process 5,000 Ceuta migrants amid local unrest
item.description: Thousands of migrants remain in the Spanish enclave, triggering anger among Ceuta residents.

item.title: Far-right UK provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos detained by ICE in US
item.description: A Trump administration official says the controversial commentator overstayed his visit in the US and will be removed.

item.title: Walmart settles US government’s opioid lawsuit
item.description: The Justice Department and Walmart confirmed the settlement without disclosing terms.

item.title: Thousands take part in March on Washington to promote voting rights
item.description: Protest draws crowds to Washington, DC amid Trump's threats of interference, voting restrictions in midterm elections.

item.title: Israeli strike kills three Palestinians in Jenin
item.description: An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians in Jenin, the first such attack in the West Bank since February 2025.

item.title: Ebola spreads to two new zones in DRC; 60 areas now affected
item.description: DRC's is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak ever recorded, with 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths.

item.title: With the US and Canada locked in a trade war, fears of a recession lurk
item.description: Analysts say Canada may lose 100,000 jobs under the current tariffs and could go into recession if the USMCA pact ends.

item.title: Before and after images show catastrophic impact of Nepal flash floods
item.description: Before-and-after satellite images reveal the scale of destruction from Nepal’s catastrophic flash floods.

item.title: RSS chief’s US visit faces protests over Hindu nationalism
item.description: Indian Hindu leader Mohan Bhagwat is due to speak in New York as human rights groups protest his visit.

item.title: 8-year-old Nepal flood survivor reunited with mother after rescue
item.description: Eight-year-old Nepal flood survivor reunited with mother after rescue

item.title: Forced birth control in Greenland violated women’s rights, experts find
item.description: Truth commission to be established after two expert reports failed to agree whether scheme constituted genocide.

item.title: Haaland and Cherki doubles send Man City to EPL win at Crystal Palace
item.description: Manchester City make it back-to-back wins to start the Premier League season as Crystal Palace slip to another defeat.

item.title: What lessons can be learned from the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster?
item.description: Scientists are looking into cause and possible link to climate change.

item.title: Timeline: Life of Ratko Mladic, general turned ‘Butcher of Bosnia’
item.description: Mladic died in prison in The Hague after failed requests by Serbian authorities to secure early release to home country.

item.title: Colombia’s new president faces backlash over ‘inhumane’ deportation policy
item.description: Less than a month into his presidency, Abelardo de la Espriella has announced effort to expel undocumented immigrants.

item.title: President Donald Trump signs order creating US Space Academy
item.description: The president said graduates of the new academy would serve the US Space Force, NASA and the civilian flight industry.

item.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy plans to hit Russia with ‘1,000 drones’ a day
item.description: Ongoing Russian attacks have killed several people and wounded dozens across Ukraine.
